---
title: "Panel coverage & variability"
subtitle: "The 222-SNP pigmentation panel read at its hg19 positions, across the modern reference and the archaics"
---

## The question

Before any pigmentation result can be trusted, the panel has to be *covered*: at each panel
SNP, how deep is the sequencing, where are the gaps, and what genotypes do the samples carry?
This page is the coverage/depth QC for the panel.

## Reading the panel at the right coordinates

The panel is defined by rsIDs, but the SGDP and archaic data are physically on **hg19/hs37d5**.
Each panel SNP therefore has to be read at its **hg19** position — a panel SNP's hg38 position
lands on the wrong base in hg19 data (for the tracer SLC24A5 that is `15:48426484` on hg19, not
the hg38 `15:48134288`). The matrices below read all 222 panel SNPs at their verified hg19
coordinates, across **159 SGDP moderns + 5 high-coverage archaics** (161 of the 222 loci are
variable and shown). Substrate + code:
[`output/panel_matrix/`](https://github.com/lasisilab/sepia/tree/main/output/panel_matrix),
[`code/export_panel_matrix.sh`](https://github.com/lasisilab/sepia/blob/main/code/export_panel_matrix.sh),
[`plan/figures/make_panel_heatmaps.R`](https://github.com/lasisilab/sepia/blob/main/plan/figures/make_panel_heatmaps.R).

## Genotype variability

Each cell is a sample's genotype at a panel SNP: homozygotes coloured by base (A/C/G/T),
heterozygotes purple, and **missing calls black**. Solid columns are monomorphic loci; mixed
columns are the variable, informative ones. Rows are individual genomes grouped by region, with
the archaics as the bottom block — where the missing calls concentrate.

![Genotype at 161 panel loci, correct hg19 coordinates. Rows = individual genomes grouped by region; homozygotes by base, het=purple, missing=black.](plan/figures/panel_atgc_heatmap.png)

## Read depth, by chromosome

Per-sample read depth at each panel SNP, log-scaled. The 159 moderns are uniformly
high-coverage (light); the 5 high-coverage archaics form the darker, more variable band at the
bottom, with genuine missing positions in black. Chromosome labels carry the panel-SNP count —
chr5 (SLC45A2) and chr15 (HERC2/OCA2/SLC24A5) hold more than half the panel, so their spans are
wide by SNP count, not chromosome length.

![Read depth (log10 DP+1) at 161 panel loci, per sample, ordered by chromosome. Missing = black.](plan/figures/panel_depth_heatmap.png)

## Reading it

- The modern reference is essentially fully covered at the panel; the coverage question is
  really about the archaics, where depth is lower and patchier — which is why a per-call
  genotype-confidence layer (depth-aware) is needed before the archaic calls are used downstream.
- **Chagyrskaya 8** is absent here (5 high-coverage archaics, not 6): its `.noRB` VCF extracts
  zero records — a known extraction bug still to fix.
- The 3 **low-coverage archaics** (Denisova 11, Goyet, Les Cottés) are BAM-only; their panel
  depth is computed separately from the read data and extends the archaic rows.
- A genome-wide depth background — to compare panel depth against the rest of the genome — is
  the natural next layer.
